newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana penis snatcher crisis worsens, seven lynched.
newsitem.headline: Ghana penis snatcher crisis worsens, seven lynched.

text.p: Mobs in Ghana's capital Accra have beaten to death seven men accused of snatching penises by witchcraft, police said late on Friday and raised the possibility the army may have to restore order.
The Police Mortuary hospital said in a statement that the death toll, which stood at two after the first lynchings on Thursday, had risen to seven.
Inspector General of Police Peter Nanfuri told state television he was prepared to call in the army to help maintain law and order in the West African nation if need be.
Victims say alleged sorcerers simply touched them to make their genitals shrink or disappear in order to extort cash in the promise of a cure.

Police and government dismiss the stories as the work of thieves, who spread rumours to create a crowd and pick pockets. Police armed with AK47 automatic rifles have been patrolling the capital's markets and bus stations.
Nanfuri said police commanders elsewhere in the former British colony had orders to be on the lookout for trouble.

Police prevented a similar lynching in the port of Tema on Friday. Saturday's Daily Graphic newspaper said a crowd built up in the town of Koforidua, 80 km (50 miles) north of Accra, on Friday, after two men reported their penises disappearing.
Medical experts have appeared on state television explaining in detail why penises increase and decrease in size. One doctor linked the phenomenon to fear.
Such reports are not uncommon in West Africa, with purported victims often blaming handshakes with sorcerers. Residents recall a similar scare in Accra in the early 1980s.
